x: Option B is incorrect: the Hazar Sutun (Hall of a Thousand Pillars) at Siri was built by Alauddin Khalji, not Sher Shah Suri. Iltutmish built the Hauz-i-Shamsi, and Alauddin built the Hauz-i-Alai and Alai Darwaza.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Tughlaqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque is Sher Shah Suri's, the Moth Masjid dates from Sikandar Lodi's reign and the Kirti Stambha is Rana Kumbha's.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque. Aibak built the Adhai Din ka Jhopra, Iltutmish completed the Qutb Minar and Alauddin Khalji built the Alai Darwaza.

s: Who built the city of Jahanpanah?
x: Jahanpanah and a fortress at Allahabad are associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Siri Fort is Alauddin's and Firoz Shah Kotla is Firoz's.

s: Who founded Siri, one of the cities of Delhi?
x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji; Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin and Jahanpanah by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: Which of the following pairs (city of Delhi – founder) is correctly matched?
x: Firozabad (Kotla) was founded by Firoz Tughlaq; Siri was Alauddin's, Tughlaqabad Ghiyasuddin's and Jahanpanah Muhammad bin Tughlaq's.

s: Who built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541) in the Purana Qila, Delhi?
x: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in 1541.

s: Who built the Jamat Khana Masjid at the Nizamuddin dargah?
x: The Jamat Khana Masjid was built by Khizr Khan, son of Alauddin Khalji.

s: Which of the following was built after Tughlaqabad Fort but before Fatehpur Sikri?
x: The Lodi Garden tombs (1451–1526) come between Tughlaqabad Fort (1320s) and Fatehpur Sikri (1570s).

s: Who built the Hazar Sutun palace at Siri?
x: Hazar Sutun, like the Alai Darwaza and Hauz-i-Alai, was built by Alauddin Khalji, not Sher Shah.

s: Who built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) at Mehrauli?
x: Balban built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) and his own tomb at Mehrauli.

s: Who added a madrasa and his own tomb at Hauz Khas, on the tank of Alauddin Khalji?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built a madrasa and his tomb at Hauz Khas beside Alauddin's tank.

s: In which citadel of Delhi stands the Ashokan pillar brought from Topra?
x: Firoz Shah Kotla, the citadel of Firozabad, holds the Topra Ashokan pillar.

s: During whose reign was the Moth ki Masjid in Delhi built?
x: The Moth ki Masjid was built in Sikandar Lodi's reign, in the Lodi style.

s: Who built the Kirti Stambha at Chittor?
x: The Kirti Stambha at Chittor is credited to Rana Kumbha of Mewar.

s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of these monuments?
1. Alai Darwaza
2. Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque
3. Sultan Garhi
4. Tughlaqabad Fort
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Sultan Garhi (1231), Alai Darwaza (1311), Tughlaqabad (1320-25) and Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541).

s: Which of the following is part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' World Heritage Site?
x: The site includes the Qutb Minar, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Alai Darwaza, Iron Pillar, Iltutmish's tomb, Alauddin's tomb and madrasa, and Imam Zamin's tomb; Tughlaqabad Fort is separate.

s: The Iron Pillar standing in the courtyard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque belongs broadly to which period?
x: The Iron Pillar is a Gupta-era pillar. Its king Chandra is generally identified with Chandragupta II, and it is famous for its resistance to rust.

s: How many tapering storeys does the Qutb Minar have?
x: The Qutb Minar has five tapering storeys, is about 72.5 metres high and bears bands of Quranic calligraphy.

s: Why does the present Qutb Minar have five storeys although its upper portion was altered?
o: Iltutmish added two storeys after completing the entire monument.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys.
Alauddin Khalji added two marble storeys to the original tower.
Sikandar Lodi added two storeys after rebuilding the monument.
x: Lightning damaged the upper portion of the Qutb Minar. Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the damaged top storey with two storeys made of marble and sandstone.

s: In which year was 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' declared a World Heritage Site?
x: The Qutb complex became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the Qutb Minar complex World Heritage Site?
x: Tughlaqabad Fort is not part of the Qutb WHS; Alai Darwaza, the Iron Pillar and Imam Zamin's tomb are.

s: Which Sultan began the Qutb Minar but built only its first storey?
x: Aibak began the minar and built the first storey; Iltutmish completed it.

s: Who built the second to fourth storeys of the Qutb Minar?
x: Iltutmish completed the second to fourth storeys; Firoz Tughlaq later rebuilt the top.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Minar:
1. Sikandar Lodi carried out repairs to it.
2. It is about 180 ft high.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sikandar Lodi, like Firoz Tughlaq, repaired the minar; it is about 238 ft (72.5 m) high, not 180 ft.

s: With whom is the king 'Chandra' of the Iron Pillar in the Qutb complex identified?
x: The Gupta-period Iron Pillar's 'Chandra' is Chandragupta II.

s: What is the approximate height of the Qutb Minar?
x: The Qutb Minar is about 72.5 m (238 ft) high; the 180 ft figure is a trap.

s: After which Sufi saint is the Qutb Minar commonly believed to be named?
x: The Qutb Minar is commonly believed to be named after Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (the point is debated).

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of monuments associated with Bengal architecture?
o: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar Fort and Ashtur tombs
Atala Masjid, Chand Minar and Gol Gumbaz
Charminar, Adina Mosque and Jami Masjid of Mandu
Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid
x: The Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid are all Bengal monuments. Option A is Bahmani (Bidar), B mixes Jaunpur, Daulatabad and Bijapur, and C mixes Hyderabad, Bengal and Mandu (Malwa).

s: Who built the Chand Minar at Daulatabad in 1435?
o: Alauddin Ahmad Shah of the Bahmani dynasty
x: The Chand Minar at Daulatabad was built in 1435 by the Bahmani Sultan Alauddin Ahmad Shah.

s: A massive propylon screen in front of the prayer hall and the absence of minarets, as seen in the Atala Masjid, mark which provincial style?
x: The Sharqi style of Jaunpur is marked by massive gateway facades with a propylon screen and no minarets, as in the Atala Masjid. Bengal used brick and curved roofs, Malwa is known for the Jami Masjid at Mandu, and Gujarat for strong Hindu-Jain carving.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Adina Mosque is associated with Pandua in Bengal, not Gujarat. Gol Gumbaz is at Bijapur, Jami Masjid at Mandu and Chand Minar at Daulatabad.

s: Which Bahmani monument has a fully covered courtyard and a large dome?
x: The Gulbarga Jama Masjid has a fully covered courtyard and a large dome; the Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is a three-storeyed building with glazed tiles.

s: The Jami Masjid at Mandu belongs to which provincial style?
x: The Jami Masjid, Mandu, is the leading monument of the Malwa style.

s: Whose tomb is the Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur?
x: Gol Gumbaz is the 17th-century tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur.

s: Strong Hindu-Jain carving is a feature of which provincial style?
x: Gujarat's provincial style shows strong Hindu-Jain carving, as in the Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad.

s: Where is the Adina Mosque located?
x: The Adina Mosque is at Pandua in Bengal, not in Gujarat.

s: Who built Rajon ki Baoli, the 'stepwell of the masons' in Mehrauli?
x: Daulat Khan Lodi built Rajon ki Baoli in 1506 under Sikandar Lodi.

s: Around which year was Rajon ki Baoli in Mehrauli built?
x: Rajon ki Baoli was built c. 1506 by Daulat Khan Lodi under Sikandar Lodi.

s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: A fully covered courtyard and a Persian madrasa
An acoustic system and piped water supply
Curved brick roofs and a Bengal-style mosque plan
x: Golconda Fort is known for its remarkable acoustics and its provision of piped water.

s: The Charminar is traditionally associated with which event?
o: The completion of the Golconda Fort water system
The founding of the Bahmani kingdom
x: The Charminar was built to mark the end of a plague. It has four arches and four minarets and combines Persian arches with Deccani stucco.

s: Who planned Hyderabad on the model of Isfahan?
x: Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad on the model of Isfahan.

s: The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh are notable because they:
o: Have no domes and are decorated only with pierced stone screens
Contain the tombs of seven Bahmani rulers and have octagonal domes on circular bases
Were built entirely in the Bengal brick tradition
Contain the tombs of seven Qutb Shahi rulers and have onion domes on square bases
x: The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh contain the seven rulers of the dynasty and are characterised by onion domes resting on square bases.

s: In which year was Hyderabad founded?
x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591, and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.

s: Which of the following describes Qutb Shahi architecture?
o: An Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions
A Buddhist-Greek style centred on stupas
A purely Persian style without Indian elements
x: Qutb Shahi architecture combined Persian and Hindu traditions and is described as an Indo-Saracenic blend.

s: In which script is the fine calligraphy on the gateway of the Golconda Jami Masjid?
x: The gateway has fine Nastaliq calligraphy (Yazdani); Naskh is used for the Quranic verses around the mihrab.

s: In which year was the Qutb Shahi capital moved from Golconda to Hyderabad?
x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591 and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.

s: In the Golconda Jami Masjid, the Quranic verses around the mihrab are in which script?
x: Naskh is used for the Quranic verses around the mihrab; the gateway is in Nastaliq.

s: By which building are the minarets of the Charminar said to have been inspired?
x: The minarets of Sultan Quli's Juma Masjid at Golconda are said to have inspired the Charminar.
